description: reconciler.py line 46 contains a tautological ternary: `return e, "noop" if e > 0 else "noop"` — both branches return the literal string "noop". The `if e > 0 else` clause is dead code and signals the author intended a distinction here (likely 'noop' when both are 0, something else when both are positive — the spec REQ-R4 says the positive case should be 'skipped_dup'; see FIND-001). This dead branch is a symptom of the FIND-001 spec violation being introduced by half-edit, and it will confuse future readers about whether the (0,0) and (positive,positive) cases were intentionally unified. Either the ternary should be simplified to `return e, "noop"` (locking in the bug for future readers), or — better — the (positive == positive) branch should be corrected to 'skipped_dup' per REQ-R4.
